name: Open-Pit Quarry
desc: Standing on the rim of an open-pit mine looking down into it — concentric benches shrink and sink ring by ring toward an acid-green pit lake, drill striations rake down every batter face, scree fans spill off the crests and a dust plume lifts off a working bench and drifts across the void; grey overburden under overcast, iron-oxide red, sodium floods on the night shift, a LiDAR point cloud, or a drafted mine plan.

energy.doc: how hard the light works — pit-lake shimmer, plume brightness, floods and the overcast sweep

scale.doc: how big the pit is — ring size and bench height (bigger scale gives fewer, more monumental benches; rebuilds the pit)

density.doc: number of benches cut into the wall

depth.doc: how deep the pit is driven — 0 is a shallow scrape, 1 is a chasm

dust.doc: airborne dust — plume volume and how much haze hangs in the pit

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default grey-limestone rock

x.doc: where the pit axis sits across the frame

y.doc: far rim height — low y buries the sky and makes the pit swallow the frame

style.doc: aesthetic: overburden = grey limestone under overcast, modelled rock; ironstone = iron-oxide red, the whole pit stained warm; nightwork = sodium floods on a night shift, dark key, the pit a void; lidar = no surfaces at all, only scan returns on an elevation ramp; mineplan = drafting ground, bench crests as line and hachures down the batters

act.doc: multi-minute programme — a working shift, a blast filling the pit with dust, or long abandonment

seed.doc: regenerates the striations, scree fans, plume source and flood positions

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
